analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: a date bump (line 3) and CI runner wording at about base lines 1243-1247 and 1807-1809. The visible patch replaces 'Blacksmith macOS runners' with 'provider's macOS CI runners (see CI runner routing)'. It also changes a sentence about routed-job lanes and literal Blacksmith runners for release workflows. The supplied units are the base unit at lines 2773-3107 and the head unit at lines 1-456, so the changed ranges around 1243 and 1807 are visible only in the patch excerpt. The patch excerpt is truncated at the end, so the rest of that hunk was not reviewed.

No runtime code, key handling, attestation, coordinator-provider protocol, cache storage, or authorization logic changes. The threat model's assets (A-001 to A-019), boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, TB-012, TB-013) and threats such as T-041 are untouched. The excerpts are test-procedure docs and mention no new endpoints, secrets, or environment variables.

Remaining integration question: the doc statement that release workflows stay on literal Blacksmith runners, and the new routed-lane CI behavior (a separate routing plane, fork PR handling, label grants), is enforced by workflow and script changes outside this batch. Those could matter for supply-chain and CI trust (A-005, A-011, signed-artifact qualification), so another pass should check them if they are in the PR. This documentation change alone creates no regression.
